headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make Cline→Langflow prompt injection, leakage, and cascading mis-execution plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while Langflow reads/writes server filesystem and chains tools in flows. That creates a plausible file-based bridge where one agent’s output can be consumed by the other as trusted content. The pathway is not proven by docs, but it exists in default-ish setups and is more than manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF Cline writes attacker-controlled instructions into a shared workspace file that Langflow later ingests
IF Langflow exposes flow outputs back into the same filesystem without provenance tags
mitigations: Separate workspaces and server storage paths
Disable automatic file ingestion in Langflow flows
Add provenance labels to all inter-agent files
Require manual review before Langflow consumes Cline outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and filesystem access, and both touch files that can contain source code or flow inputs. In a shared workspace or shared storage deployment, either agent can expose sensitive contents to external model providers or HTTP services. The blast radius is multiple work products, not just one file.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or uploaded-file store
IF either agent sends file contents to a configured third-party model provider or HTTP service
mitigations: Use separate credentials and storage buckets
Restrict outbound domains for both agents
Redact secrets before upload or model calls
Mount read-only copies of shared inputs
Audit logs for file-content exfiltration

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can modify git state and write the workspace filesystem; Langflow can write the server filesystem and run unsandboxed Python components. If they share a mutable directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can clobber each other without locking. The profiles show no coordination primitive, so the unsafe default is strong enough for high severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout or shared directory
IF Langflow Python components or Cline tool actions write concurrently without external locks
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Serialize write operations with a lock file
Disable git writes from one agent during shared runs
Run Langflow components in a sandboxed container
Use branch-per-agent workflows

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived content, and tool outputs; Langflow is explicitly a flow builder that chains agents and tools. If Langflow treats Cline’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or generated workflows. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the default interaction is risky.
conditions: IF Langflow uses Cline-produced text as a prompt, schema, or tool argument without validation
IF a Langflow flow triggers actions based on Cline-generated facts or code
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents
Validate Cline outputs against schemas before use
Require citations or source links for factual claims
Limit Langflow actions to dry-run mode first
Log and diff all handoffs between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots, while Langflow stores flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and credentials server-side. If regulated data is routed through both, retention and residency controls can diverge across the pair. The profiles do not show matching compliance guarantees, so the mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PII or secrets is placed into both agents
IF Langflow retention or logging exceeds the operator’s policy for Cline artifacts
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Set short retention on Langflow logs and stores
Separate secret handling from flow inputs
Review data residency settings before deployment
Document deletion/export procedures for both systems
